value.rationale: Cubic terms are the first nonzero local truncation error of centered differences. The result gives the exact geometric split of full-frame stochastic error and the complete zero-variance cases; most importantly, it reveals and quantifies a strict, noiseless, positive-radius MSE optimum for undercomplete orthogonal frames. The sharp \(d/k\) improvement is achieved on a globally strongly convex polynomial, so the phenomenon is relevant to safe derivative-free gradient estimation rather than a degeneracy of an ill-posed objective. The result supplies interpretable structural and finite-sample benchmarks even without a downstream convergence theorem.
